transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-10 14:00 PST
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Location: Zoom
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Leah (CSM), Tom (CTO, Evercrest), Aisha (Head of ML), Ravi (Security), Nora (Product)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i know there's a lot to get through so we'll try to keep it tight. quick round robin — say hi and roles?
[00:12] Tom: Tom lee, CTO at Evercrest, i'll be the exec sponsor.
[00:16] Aisha: Aisha, head of ML, i'll own model eval and integration.
[00:21] Ravi: ravi, security, i'll drive compliance and network reqs.
[00:26] Nora: nora product, prioritized use cases and rollout plan.
[00:30] Maya: great, from redwood we have carlos on the infra/arch side and leah on success. carlos, quick intro?
[00:36] Carlos: hey all, carlos nguyen, solutions eng. i focus on private/dedicated deployments and perf tuning — happy to walk network/topology and batching strategies.
[00:44] Leah: hi everyone, leah ortiz, csm — i'll coordinate pilots and acceptance criteria.

[00:52] Maya: objective today: align on pilot scope (8 weeks), deployment mode (we're proposing dedicated capacity in your VPC), security checklist, and success metrics. also surface any hard blockers. quick validation: is dedicated behind your VPC what you were expecting?
[01:10] Tom: yes we wanted predictable throughput; hosted api is fine for a POC but for production we need isolation and predictable tail latency.
[01:18] Aisha: and we need consistent latency p95 under 200ms for short queries, and accuracy regression below 3% on our evaluation sets.
[01:27] Ravi: security-wise we require bring-your-own-kms, SAML SSO, RBAC and audit logs retained for 1 year, plus option for HSM for key custody. also we'll need SOC2 and ISO docs plus pen test history.

[01:40] Carlos: absolutely — for dedicated we can run a private control plane and place runtime nodes in your VPC via peering or transit gateway. BYOK/KMS integration is supported; we also have HSM integrations for enterprise customers. note: there are a few networking patterns — we can do cross-account roles with endpoints or colocated subnets.
[01:58] Ravi: when you say private control plane, is any token or payload leaving our VPC? we need to know data plane boundaries.
[02:06] Carlos: good question — data plane (inference requests) stays in your VPC. control plane metadata (billing, orchestration) flows to our managed control plane unless you opt for private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed. for this pilot we can do private control plane mode if that's a hard requirement, but it extends setup time by ~2 weeks.
[02:28] Tom: timeline wise we want a pilot that can be production-adjacent, but not block us. if private control plane adds two weeks, that's OK as long as we start pre-work now.

[02:40] Maya: propose this: 8-week pilot with dedicated nodes in your VPC, start with managed control plane and option to switch to private control plane mid-pilot if needed; SOW will call this out as a milestone. does that sound workable?
[02:55] Nora: i like starting with managed cp for speed but want the option to flip. is there an impact to performance or compliance?
[03:02] Carlos: performance is the same; compliance differs only in control plane access and audit custody. if you need full control we can package the private control plane, but ops overhead increases.

[03:15] Aisha: on the ML side, what model variants are available? we plan to run a quantized open model — cost is a big driver.
[03:24] Carlos: we support multiple open models, quantized variants, and recommend a 4-bit quantized variant for inference to reduce costs. batching and KV cache will help with throughput. note that certain kernels perform better on A100 vs H100; if you have dedicated GPU type preferences we'll note them in SOW.
[03:45] Aisha: our internal perf budget assumes ~12k tokens/min peak across 3 routes — can you model cost for that?
[03:52] Maya: we'll include a cost model in the SOW. quick aside: token accounting can be noisy in early runs — we'll share guidance on prompt engineering to limit token churn.

[04:05] Ravi: retention and logs — we need audit logs, request traces (anonymized), and the ability to revoke keys immediately. is tokenization of logs automatic?
[04:14] Carlos: we redact PII by default in logs unless you opt-in; audit logs are immutable and can be routed to your S3 or SIEM. key revocation is supported via KMS; if you use an external HSM there are additional rotation steps.

[04:27] Maya: i'll attach our security pack link after the call: https://redwood.example/security/evercrest (note: placeholder). that'll include SOC2 reports, architectural diagrams, and the network checklist.

[04:40] Nora: onboarding tasks — who will own integration pieces?
[04:44] Leah: leah will coordinate runbooks and staging access. carlos will own network design and runtime tuning. maya will own commercial and SOW.

[04:55] Tom: success criteria — let's make them concrete so we can sign off. proposed: (1) end-to-end P95 latency for primary route < 200ms, (2) quality regressions below 3% vs baseline on our eval set, (3) ops integration: SSO + RBAC configured and logs flowing to our SIEM, (4) cost within 15% of the modeled estimate.
[05:20] Maya: agreed — we'll add those as acceptance criteria in the SOW.

[05:28] Aisha: curious about fallback policies — can we have a lower-cost model route if capacity or cost overshoots?
[05:34] Carlos: yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallbacks. you can route by latency, cost, or region. we can configure a canary or hybrid route and automatically fallback to a small cheaper quantized variant.

[05:48] Nora: do you have an eval harness we can run against our test corpus? we want reproducible scoring.
[05:53] Maya: yes, redwood optimize includes eval tooling and a prompt set runner — we'll share a lightweight harness and CI runner. for the pilot we can help set up a daily regression check and alert thresholds.

[06:08] Tom: what about telemetry — token-level costs per route and tracing?
[06:12] Carlos: console shows token breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and trace links. we'll add custom tags for your request ids so it links to your logs.

[06:24] Ravi: network specifics — we need IP ranges for allowlisting and a plan for egress.
[06:29] Carlos: i'll send IP ranges and two recommended patterns: (1) private ENIs in your account, or (2) cross-account peering with NAT. ENIs give tighter control.

[06:40] Maya: ok action items — we'll summarize after. any other blockers?
[06:45] Aisha: one more technical — warmup / KV cache priming. cold-start token rates are high on some flows. can you help with priming strategies?
[06:53] Carlos: yes, we can pre-warm KV caches and set warm-up batches during off hours. we'll add priming steps in the runbook. note: warmup affects cost but reduces p95 spikes.

[07:06] Nora: what about governance — who gets access to which routes; we need RBAC that mirrors our environment.
[07:12] Leah: RBAC maps to SAML groups; we'll provide templates to map roles to groups, and we can demo that in the VPC walkthrough.

[07:24] Tom: timeline — we want pilot kickoff next week. what's a realistic start date?
[07:29] Maya: if we get SOW signed and network prework done this week, we can begin staging setup by 12/16, and start traffic tests week of 12/21. that checks out with an 8-week runway into early Feb.

[07:45] Ravi: pen testing — do you run pentests on your infra? we may want an external pentest during pilot.
[07:50] Carlos: we run internal security scans and have prior external tests; happy to coordinate a scoped external pentest on the customer-facing surfaces. we'll note that in SOW and schedule.

[08:04] Maya: ok final recap: Redwood to send SOW with pilot milestones, cost model, and security pack; Redwood to schedule VPC walkthrough and provide IP ranges; Evercrest to share prompt set and perf targets; mutual agreement on acceptance criteria (latency, quality, RBAC/logging, cost).

[08:27] Tom: thanks everyone — appreciate the clarity. i'll aim to review SOW within 48 hours.
[08:32] Maya: great — we'll follow up with calendar invites for VPC and a draft SOW. thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic captions had some mis-hears — e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Sage maker" split, and occasional dropped punctuation. Speaker labels were accurate apart from brief crosstalk at 03:02-03:15.
questions: Is private control plane required for pilot?
What are the exact latency and quality acceptance thresholds?
Who owns key rotation and HSM custody during pilot?
